question: May a group of citizens organised as an energy community own or lease the local distribution network, and what must Member States then ensure?
reply: {"gold_answers": "yes", "gold_reason": "Article 16(2)(b) lets Member States provide that citizen energy communities may own, establish, purchase or lease distribution networks and manage them autonomously. Article 16(4)(a)-(c) lists what Member States must then ensure: an operation agreement with the DSO/TSO, appropriate network charges accounting separately for fed-in and consumed electricity, and no discrimination against or harm to customers who stay connected to the distribution system.", "other_articles": [], "ambiguity": "none", "ambiguity_reason": "The question maps directly onto Article 16(2)(b) and Article 16(4). verdict.gold_reason: Article 16(2)(b) lets Member States provide that citizen energy communities may own, establish, purchase or lease distribution networks and manage them autonomously. Article 16(4)(a)-(c) lists what Member States must then ensure: an operation agreement with the DSO/TSO, appropriate network charges accounting separately for fed-in and consumed electricity, and no discrimination against or harm to customers who stay connected to the distribution system.
verdict.ambiguity_reason: The question maps directly onto Article 16(2)(b) and Article 16(4). No other article addresses community ownership of distribution networks.
